issues.title: Tensor-product basis index
issues.failure_explanation: For d=2 and identity operators, the old construction maps H_{k_1}(x_1)H_{k_2}(x_2) to H_{k_1}(x_1)H_{k_1}(x_2), ignoring k_2. Consequently it does not implement the claimed coordinatewise tensor action, and the asserted product norm and continuous extension do not follow from the literal definition.
issues.overall_effect: The literal operator used to define the Smolyak quadrature and interpolation constructions has the wrong action, leaving the listed sparse-grid lower and upper results unsupported until the index is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace H_{k_1} by H_{k_j} in the j-th factor of the tensor-product basis action. The resulting coordinatewise definition has the asserted product norm and continuous extension, so all listed Smolyak quadrature and interpolation results can use the operator without further changes.
issues.why_classification: The independently indexed input basis, the tensor-product notation, and the immediately asserted product-norm identity uniquely force the j-th operator to act on H_{k_j}. No inference, construction, hypothesis, or guarantee must be changed; k_1 is a transcriptional index slip.

issues.title: Fooling-function Sobolev normalization
issues.failure_explanation: The old proof computes the norm of h_Lambda as the square root of the sum of squared derivative norms, but eq:1d-RHS and the ensuing lower-bound invocation divide by the unsquared sum. Those expressions cannot be the claimed error-to-norm quotient, so the theorem's reduction to the univariate normalized lower bound is invalid as written.
issues.overall_effect: The general sparse-grid lower-bound proof, its isotropic specialization, and the interpolation lower-bound argument lack the stated normalized fooling-function estimate until the denominator is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing exponent 1/2 on the sum of squared derivative norms in eq:1d-RHS and in the corresponding displayed invocation of the univariate estimate. This makes the denominator equal to the already computed Sobolev norm of h_Lambda and restores the same normalized estimate in the general lower bound, its isotropic specialization, and the interpolation argument.
issues.why_classification: The old proof itself computes the norm as the square root of the displayed sum, so the normalized quotient uniquely forces this correction. It is a repeated transcriptional omission of an exponent, with no new estimate, proof step, weakening, or change of rate required.

issues.title: Isotropic Smolyak fresh-node count
issues.failure_explanation: The old hypotheses impose exponential bounds but do not require distinct quadrature orders or disjoint node sets. Nevertheless, the proof asserts that the actual number N of evaluations equals the sum of the products of all n-level counts. For example, the admissible choice n_l=2^l-1 consists of odd orders, whose Hermite node sets all contain zero, so the displayed sum counts an already available node repeatedly. Adjacent equal orders, also permitted by the old hypotheses, can additionally make a level difference vanish. Thus the exact identity and the resulting lower comparison between N and the level parameters are not justified.
issues.overall_effect: The logarithmically enhanced isotropic lower bound, and the isotropic part of the interpolation theorem that invokes it, are not established for the old evaluation count and full class of allowed order sequences.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the level orders to be pairwise distinct and count fresh nodes rather than summing all level sizes. If X_l is the Gauss–Hermite node set and m_l is the cardinality of X_l minus all lower-level node sets, then distinct Hermite polynomials share at most the node zero, so n_l−1 ≤ m_l ≤ n_l. Use N = sum over the isotropic index set of the products of the m_l values to recover N comparable to M^L L^{d−1}, and apply the analogous fresh-node count to the interpolation nodes. This restores both logarithmically enhanced lower bounds for the standard nondegenerate level hierarchy.
issues.why_classification: The false cardinality identity is used essentially and is not a notational slip. A complete repair requires a fresh-node decomposition and a common-root argument, together with a limited restriction excluding repeated orders that can make level differences vanish. This work is contained and preserves the method, polynomial rate, logarithmic factor, and downstream interpolation result for a recognizably comparable standard class, so it avoids serious loss but exceeds a routine same-scope minor repair.

issues.title: Affine-lattice truncation radius
issues.failure_explanation: Already for d=1, choose a fixed nonnegative nonzero smooth function psi supported in (1,2) and set f_b(x)=psi(b(x-b)). Every affine quadrature node lies in [-b,b], so Q_N(f_b)=0. Directly from the old Gaussian weight and Sobolev norm, I(f_b) is comparable to exp(-b^2/2)/b, while the norm is comparable to exp(-b^2/4)b^{alpha-1/2}; hence the normalized error is comparable to exp(-b^2/4)b^{-alpha-1/2}. With the old b^2=(alpha/2) ln N, this has polynomial size N^{-alpha/8}, far above the claimed N^{-alpha} times a logarithm. Thus the proposition itself is false at the old truncation scale.
issues.overall_effect: The affine rank-1 lattice rate and the corresponding branch of the QMC summary theorem fail for the stated old radius.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated radius by b = (2+η)√(α ln N) for any fixed η>0 and include the truncation/discretization balance supplied by the scaled-lattice estimate. In particular, choose β with 1/(2+η)^2 ≤ β < 1/4 so that exp(−βb^2) ≤ N^−α; the remaining powers of b give the stated logarithmic exponent. The affine-lattice branch of the QMC summary then retains the same N^−α rate, with a constant allowed to depend on η.
issues.why_classification: The counterexample rules out the old radius, and the source does not uniquely force a one-symbol correction. Restoring the result requires changing the executable truncation parameter and rebalancing the lattice and Gaussian-tail errors. That is a contained reoptimization preserving the same function class, method architecture, polynomial rate, and logarithmic guarantee, so it is moderate rather than serious, but it is more than a routine minor edit.

issues.title: Bell-recurrence regularity hypothesis
issues.failure_explanation: For the nontrivial case r=1 and eta=1, the old lemma permits a differentiable Phi without a second derivative, while C_{2,1} and C'_{1,1} both require Phi''. More generally, the proof explicitly uses Phi^(r-eta+2). Thus the recurrence is not even defined for all inputs admitted by the old statement.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma overclaims applicability to merely differentiable maps. Its later chain-rule use already assumes enough C^alpha regularity, so no later formal result depends on the defective extra scope.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the lemma’s hypothesis to require the derivatives that occur in the recurrence; for the nontrivial case 1 ≤ η ≤ r, it suffices to assume that Φ is (r−η+2)-times differentiable. Then C_{r+1,η} and C'_{r,η} are defined and the existing Bell-polynomial calculation proves the same identity.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine missing regularity premise rather than a transcriptional error, but the needed order is read directly from the displayed terms and adding it is a short, standard smoothness qualification. The recurrence and proof are otherwise unchanged, and later uses already impose sufficient C^α regularity, so no downstream statement or substantive guarantee is lost.

issues.title: Digital-net transformed-norm homogeneity
issues.failure_explanation: For a nonzero f, replacing f by c f also replaces g by c g. The left side of the old estimate therefore scales as c^2, whereas its right side scales as c, so no f-independent constant can make the displayed inequality hold for all c. The preceding derivative bound instead yields a right side proportional to the square of the H_rho^alpha norm.
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not produce the linear transformed-norm estimate needed for the digital-net error, leaving that proposition and the corresponding optimal branch of the QMC summary unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the final transformed-norm-squared estimate to have C_{d,α} times the square of the H_rho^alpha norm of f on its right-hand side. Squaring and summing eq:D_g_bound gives exactly this estimate; taking square roots then yields the required linear bound on the transformed unanchored Sobolev norm and restores the digital-net proposition and its summary-theorem branch.
issues.why_classification: Both homogeneity and the preceding derivative estimate uniquely force the missing square. The corrected line immediately yields the intended linear norm bound after taking a square root, with no new argument, weakened guarantee, or change of rate, so the defect is transcriptional.
